scope: Primary-literature comparison with the completed frozen-field study; no new simulation or solver change

case.profile: Uniform physical density, constant elliptical cross-section, sharp ends, open space
case.observable: Raw lab electric field at matched material points; not a reference-subtracted or complete Lorentz-force tracking benchmark

source_families: Traditional independent transverse Poisson slices, with differing optional longitudinal closures
Local equivalent line-density-gradient field with profile/boundary/averaging-dependent g
Common-potential symplectic 2.5D models with longitudinal kicks and reference-scale matching
Nonlocal longitudinal impedance/Green-function methods retaining finite transverse extent
Curved-orbit remapping and curved-Poisson corrections, which are separate requirements
interpretation: The current hard-ended case exposes limitations of this particular local closure; it does not invalidate every method called 2.5D.

Global slenderness does not supply slow longitudinal variation at a sharp end. Changing a finite constant g cannot create the finite-width interior end-field tail where resolved lambda-prime vanishes.
The cited PyHEADTAIL paper uses 6.36 in one free-space example. The accompanying thesis gives a shape-dependent free-space g0. Neither establishes a universal OpenG0=6.36 for our elliptical source.
Round-pipe on-axis, transverse-average, equivalent-ellipsoid and constant-density-radius-variation g conventions differ and must not be mixed.

The native transverse refinement is stable and bulk fields are close on the stated characteristic scale. That scale is unsuitable as the sole accuracy criterion for the much smaller midpoint curvature field.
Small a/R is a local condition, distinct from total bunch angle L/R. The 143-degree extent alone does not invalidate a local Frenet expansion.
Qiang's 2025 published paper and updated 2026 preprint must be distinguished. The latter adds explicit r0 matching to the 3D longitudinal Gaussian field.

The displayed regularized curvature correction has zero radial derivative on axis. This is our mathematical inference, not a stated intentional reference-force subtraction. Quantitative finite-arc hoop-field comparison needs matched global boundary conditions and field/force conventions.
Numerical vacuum padding and physical outer matching are different issues. The exact matched straight constant-tube and padding controls have not yet been run.
The new accepted FFA paper has only an accessible abstract here. Its detailed parameters and quantitative accuracy are not inferred from that abstract or from an older proceedings paper.
